predecessors.name: Syria
predecessors.text: Aleppo, where rebel fighters 'violently penetrated into the city' on 19 July 2012, and Manbij, which fell on 20 July 2012

successors.name: Syria
successors.text: Idlib and the towns taken in the 2024 offensive: 'Opposition forces captured the capital Damascus on 8 December' 2024

ledger.x: 2012: the rebels hold Eastern Ghouta.
2012: Al-Rastan is in the rebels' hands before the state's first dated event (Aleppo, 19 July).
19 July 2012: rebels from the northern countryside enter Aleppo and the city divides.
19 July 2012 to December 2016: Aleppo is a front line.
20 July 2012: Manbij falls to the rebels.
July 2012: al-Bab falls to the Free Syrian Army.
February 2013: Shaddadi falls to the al-Nusra Front.
6 March 2013: Raqqa falls to the rebels.
July 2013: ISIS takes Shaddadi.
November 2013: ISIS holds al-Bab.
January 2014: ISIL takes Manbij.
14 January 2014: ISIL takes Raqqa from the rebels.
February to May 2014: the Southern Front's Quneitra offensive.
28 March 2015: rebels take Idlib.

June 2015: the page gives the rebel share at this date, not a capture date: 'By June 2015, the Southern Front controlled about 70 percent of Daraa Governorate' (IISS); Bosra fell on 25 March and the Nasib crossing on 1 April 2015.
22 December 2016: the front in Aleppo closes.
22 December 2016: the government retakes Aleppo, 'what had been Syria's largest city before the war'.
2017: the Syrian Salvation Government, a Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham-led administration, begins to govern Idlib: it 'governed the region from 2017 until 2024'.
18 February 2018: the government offensive on Eastern Ghouta opens with heavy bombardment; the ground assault began on 25 February.
14 April 2018: Eastern Ghouta falls.
April 2018: Eastern Ghouta returns to the government.

15 May 2018: 'The Syrian government retook control of the city on 15 May 2018 as part of an agreement'; the rebels surrendered the territory and their heavy weapons for safe passage to rebel-held northern Syria.
18 June 2018: 'On 18 June, during the night, the Syrian Army captured several farms near Busra Al-Harir and Masekah' (Daraa, 'rebel-held areas in the eastern part of the Daraa Governorate').

By 23 July 2018 'the forces of the Southern Front were fully defeated and lost all territory that was under their control'; the 2018 Southern Syria offensive page cites SOHR for the government taking all opposition-held Daraa on 19 July and 'the entire Quneitra Province' on 31 July (reference titles).
July 2018: the south returns to the government; the Quneitra rebels left for Idlib after an evacuation agreement on 20 July.
27 and 29 November 2024: the opposition offensive.
7 and 8 December 2024: 'On 7 December, rebel forces entered Damascus.
8 December 2024: the opposition wins.

wars.name: Syrian civil war
wars.outcome: The opposition held Aleppo's east (2012-2016), Raqqa (March 2013 to January 2014), Idlib (from March 2015) and Eastern Ghouta (2012-April 2018) and won on 8 December 2024 when the Assad government fell.

wars.name: Battle of Aleppo (2012-2016)
wars.outcome: Syrian Arab Army and allied victory: the city was divided from July 2012 and the east was retaken by 22 December 2016.

wars.name: Rif Dimashq offensive (February-April 2018)
wars.outcome: Syrian Army-allied victory: 18 February to 14 April 2018; Eastern Ghouta evacuated.

wars.name: Second Battle of Idlib
wars.outcome: Rebel victory: 24 to 28 March 2015, Idlib city in rebel hands.

wars.name: Battle of Raqqa (2013)
wars.outcome: Rebel victory: 3 to 6 March 2013; Raqqa fell on 6 March.

wars.name: 2018 Southern Syria offensive
wars.outcome: Syrian Army-allied victory: the offensive opened on 18 June 2018 and by 23 July the Southern Front had lost all its territory (Southern Front page).

certainty.note: Front lines moved by town and the pages give towns, not lines; the rebel pockets are drawn from the gazetteer's discs and admin1 units.
